questions.subject: ANALYTICAL_CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: calculate expected precipitate mass in gravimetry
questions.stem: A 0.892 g sample contains 32.4 percent analyte. If the gravimetric factor converting analyte to precipitate is 0.635, what mass of precipitate is expected?

options.misconception: omits the gravimetric factor entirely
divides by the gravimetric factor instead of multiplying
forgets to convert the percentage to a fraction

questions.explanation: The analyte mass is the sample mass times the percent as a fraction. Multiplying by the gravimetric factor converts that analyte mass into the mass of the weighed precipitate form. Dividing by the factor or ignoring it misstates the precipitate mass.
questions.hint: Sample mass times fraction gives analyte, times factor gives precipitate.
